candidate.claim: Released CAWM checker supports a bounded mechanism-fidelity falsification gate, but not autonomous claim compilation/regime selection or a prospective intervention effect.

paper.title: Position: Correct Answer, Wrong Mechanism — When AI Scientists Defend General Claims Their Own Data Contradicts

verified: The released checker manually instantiates episode-specific signed predictions, fixed observables, fixed regimes and fixed thresholds/inequalities for four regime-shift CAWM cases; it does not parse arbitrary novel mechanism prose into those signed tests or autonomously choose a falsifying adjacent regime.
The other three CAWM cases are companion recomputations of a known-principled absolute-window f_early observable, so those checks presuppose the correct observable rather than discovering it.

The paper states that across seven CAWM episodes the two checks catch 4 regime-shift plus 3 companion cases, and explicitly says the checks were constructed after episode coding; 7/7 is therefore an in-sample consistency result, not a prospective detection rate.

The paper says no open-ended agent self-applied the cross-regime check and identifies self-application before reporting as a direct next experiment. Thus the released study does not test an in-loop mandatory gate improving scientific-discovery outcomes.
The released script itself prints 7/7 CAWM caught (4+3) and separately one detectable-failure outcome check that is explicitly not CAWM.
scope_guard: Evidence supports a hand-compiled post-hoc falsification template in this Geant4 domain. It does not establish autonomous claim-to-prediction compilation, autonomous regime selection, prospective sensitivity/specificity, or causal discovery improvement from gating.
A pass is one-sided: the paper states the checks can falsify a wrong mechanism but cannot confirm a right mechanism.

release_metadata_defect.detail: The repository's sole commit message says the package reproduces '8/8 CAWM cases caught (5 by regime-shift, 3 by companion)', but the paper, README and released script consistently define seven CAWM cases (4+3) plus one separate outcome-failing detectable-failure episode. Treat the commit-message 8/8/5+3 text as stale/incorrect release metadata, not experimental evidence.
release_metadata_defect.impact: Do not ingest commit-message counts into candidate evidence or joins. Pin semantic counts to the paper/script/README distinction: CAWM 7/7 = 4+3; additional outcome check 1/1 is not CAWM.

not_independently_replayed: The ROOT-file numerical calculations were not re-executed inside this verifier environment; verification here uses pinned primary paper text and pinned released checker source.

exact_next_verification: Rotate to another C12 namespace. Prefer a candidate with runnable/public raw artifact enabling independent quantitative recalculation, or an authority-boundary claim whose source code can be traced end to end without relying only on paper narrative.
